rationale: The original2011 city rules establish distinct implementation regimes and statutory assignment. Shanghai targets defined new purchases by local/nonlocal families with combined family-area and residency exemptions. Chongqing covers nine urban districts, includes pre-existing detached commercial homes, new high-price homes and a defined nonlocal ordinary-home category, with different property-level area allowances and reference-price rules. These change actual treatment, exemptions, geographic scope and required joins; they are not splits by outcome, rate bracket or paper result. The shared paper estimates separate city counterfactuals. Both records retain the same publication DOI and the working-version evidence boundary.

The implemented experiment has two different assignments. The invitation case compares recruited firms randomly offered meetings with no-meetings firms. The peer-composition case is nested within invited firms: random ranks conditional on26 subregions and baseline size-sector strata fill predefined group slots. It compares feasible peer compositions, not invitation arms, and requires original group rosters, peer baseline employment and allocation expectations. The author registry documents both interventions and the final paper II.B and III.B specifies different allocation and estimators. Four group types, outcomes and expected/surprise specifications remain within one peer case; none creates another variation. Original DOI and invitation maturity are preserved.
